## Saturation adjustment at fixed temperature and pressure (`ThermoX.forward`) {#sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp}

### Summary

Given a temperature, a pressure and the mole fractions of all species, this solver moves material between gases
and condensates until every reaction of @sec-ch04-conditions satisfies its two-sided condition. It is the
equilibrium step a host code takes when it knows $T$ and $p$ (a prescribed sounding, the trial temperatures of an
adiabat, the output of a dynamical step that updates pressure and temperature first), and it is called inside every
pass of the entropy and adiabat routines of @sec-ch03. The method is a Newton iteration on the reaction extents
in which each step is a small constrained least-squares problem: the linearised residuals of the active reactions
are driven to zero subject to no species going negative, a per-reaction clip to the stock a step consumes, and a
line search that keeps every gas positive. Convergence is quadratic once the active set is right, and the solver
returns the Jacobian of the residuals with respect to the extents, the gain matrix, which @sec-ch03-adiabat needs.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Solve @eq-ch04-conditions-complementarity at fixed $(T, p)$ by the Newton step @eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-newton
on the extents of the active reactions.

**Data.** In: $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $x_i$ of all species (last axis), in place; out: adjusted $x_i$, the gain matrix
$\mathsf G$ $(\dots, N_{\mathrm r}, N_{\mathrm r})$ [-], the diagnostic `diag` $(\dots, 1)$.

**Placement.** `ThermoX.forward`, one call per set of cells; the per-cell kernel is `equilibrate_tp`.

**Activation.** Whenever the card has nucleation reactions (no reactions: a no-op returning an empty tensor).
`max-iter` (default 10) bounds the outer passes, `ftol` (default $10^{-6}$) is the tolerance on $r_j$; `warm_start`
reuses the last active set (@sec-ch04-drivers).

**Guarantee / limits.** Mole fractions stay non-negative and sum to one; a converged cell has $|r_j| \le$ `ftol` for
every active reaction and the complementarity of the rest; a cell that does not converge is returned partially
adjusted with `diag` $< 0$.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: 2000 random Jupiter-like cells, CPU equals CUDA to $10^{-10}$ with eight
condensables, convergence on the last allowed iteration.
:::

Local symbols: $\xi_j$ the extent of reaction $j$ per mole of parcel [-]; $\boldsymbol\xi$ the vector over the active
reactions; $\mathsf W$ the weight matrix, $W_{ji} = \partial r_j/\partial x_i$; $\mathsf G = \mathsf W\mathsf N$ the
gain matrix with $\mathsf N$ the stoichiometric matrix restricted to the active reactions, $G_{jk} = \partial r_j/\partial\xi_k$;
$\theta_i$ the per-species stock factor and $\lambda$ the line-search factor [-]; $K_{\max}$ the outer iteration
cap (`max-iter`). The internal names are `weight`, `gain`, `rhs` (the right-hand side, overwritten by the solved
extents), `theta`, `lambda`, `reaction_set` and `nactive`.

### Derivation

**The linear system.** Along the reaction extents the mole fractions change by $\mathrm dx_i = \sum_k \nu_{ik}\,\mathrm d\xi_k$
(before renormalisation), so the residual @eq-ch04-conditions-residual-x of reaction $j$ changes by
$\mathrm dr_j = \sum_i W_{ji}\,\mathrm dx_i = \sum_k G_{jk}\,\mathrm d\xi_k$ with
$$
W_{ji} = \frac{\partial r_j}{\partial x_i} = \frac{a_{ij}}{x_i} - \frac{A_j}{x_{\mathrm g}} \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad
W_{ji} = 0 \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad
G_{jk} = \sum_{i} W_{ji}\,\nu_{ik} .
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-weight}
The $-A_j/x_{\mathrm g}$ term is the derivative of the gas normalisation: every gas, including an inert one with
$a_{ij} = 0$, dilutes the partial pressures. @eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-weight is computed in `equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}) as the array `weight` and the product `mmdot(gain, weight,
stoich_active)`; for an absent gas reactant the $1/x_i$ is replaced by the bounded $1/r^\star$ of
@sec-ch04-conditions. The Newton step for the active reactions is then the square linear system
$$
\mathsf G\,\Delta\boldsymbol\xi = -\mathbf r ,
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-newton}
which `equilibrate_tp` solves not directly but as the constrained least-squares problem below; for one active
reaction the gain is the scalar $G = \sum_i (a_i/x_i - A/x_{\mathrm g})\nu_i$ and the step is $-r/G$ (`[C1]` of
`equilibrate_tp_check.py`, which verifies the derivative symbolically).

**The constraints.** A step must not drive any species negative: $x_i + \sum_k \nu_{ik}\Delta\xi_k \ge 0$. The
kernel hands @eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-newton with these $N$ inequality rows to `leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin`
({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin >}}), the active-set solver of @sec-ch10 for
$\min\|\mathsf G\Delta\boldsymbol\xi + \mathbf r\|_2$ subject to $-\mathsf N\Delta\boldsymbol\xi \le \mathbf x$: the
origin $\Delta\boldsymbol\xi = 0$ is feasible by construction (the bounds are the current amounts), the solver adds
the single most violated bound that is linearly independent of the already active ones per inner iteration, and
holds an active single-species bound exactly on its value (so that a species that must be used up is used up to
the last bit, not to within round-off). The inner iteration budget is $\max(N + 1, K_{\max})$, independent of the
outer one. The method is the active-set strategy for inequality-constrained least squares of Nocedal and Wright
([Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., 2006](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5), chapter 16) in the
non-negative least-squares tradition of Lawson and Hanson
([Solving Least Squares Problems, 1995](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611971217), chapter 23); the KKT system itself,
its scaling and its direct solve are the subject of @sec-ch10.

**Limiter and line search.** The solver does not enforce a bound that is linearly dependent on the active block
(two condensates drawing on one vapour), so the kernel clips every reaction to the stock of what it consumes:
$$
\theta_i = \min\Bigl(1, \frac{x_i}{\sum_k \max(0, -\nu_{ik}\Delta\xi_k)}\Bigr), \qquad
\Delta\xi_k \leftarrow \Delta\xi_k \min_{i:\,\nu_{ik}\Delta\xi_k < 0} \theta_i ,
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-limiter}
with no credit for what another reaction produces at the same time. @eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-limiter is computed in
`equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}) as the arrays `theta` and the per-reaction
`lam`. The update is then applied with a factor $\lambda$ that is halved until every gas stays strictly positive
(a gas that was positive may not land exactly on zero), after which the mole fractions are renormalised to sum to
one, which matters whenever $\sum_i \nu_{ij} \ne 0$ and leaves every mole ratio unchanged (`[C4]`):
$$
x_i \leftarrow \frac{x_i + \lambda\sum_k \nu_{ik}\Delta\xi_k}{\sum_l \bigl(x_l + \lambda\sum_k \nu_{lk}\Delta\xi_k\bigr)} .
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-update}
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-update is computed in the same `equilibrate_tp`. A $\lambda$ that underflows is a failure
(status 4).

**What the iteration returns.** On exit, with the final composition, the active set is recomputed with the
equilibrium test $|r_j| \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ and the gain of exactly those reactions is assembled and
scattered into the $N_{\mathrm r} \times N_{\mathrm r}$ output, zero outside the active block; this $\mathsf G$ is what
`effective_cp` of @sec-ch03-adiabat inverts. The diagnostic is the iteration count on success and
$-(100\,s + n)$ on failure, with status $s = 20$ for the iteration cap and $s \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ for the solver's own
codes or $4$ for the line search (`[C5]`); convergence on the last allowed pass counts as success. What is exact:
the renormalised update conserves every mole ratio and the complementarity at convergence holds to
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ in the log quotient. What is approximate: the linearisation; the iteration is Newton's
method with quadratic convergence near the solution (`[C2]`: the ratio $|r_{k+1}|/r_k^2$ stays below one on the
water example) and a damped first phase while far from it, because the step on the logarithmic residual changes a
small vapour fraction by at most a factor of about $1 + |r|$ per pass (`[C3]`). The check is
`equilibrate_tp_check.py`, a numpy port of the kernel for one reaction.

### Numerical method

One outer pass, for one cell, in the order the kernel runs it:

1. Compute the shifted curves $L_j - A_j\ln p$ once per call ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}).
2. For every reaction in the current `reaction_set`, evaluate $r_j$; put the reaction in the active block if the
   test of @sec-ch04-conditions says so, otherwise swap it to the back of the set. The active block is the first
   `nactive` entries.
3. If the block is empty, stop: converged (also when this happens on the last allowed pass).
4. Assemble $\mathsf W$ for the block and $\mathsf G = \mathsf W\mathsf N$; solve the constrained least-squares problem
   for $\Delta\boldsymbol\xi$ ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin >}}).
5. Apply the stock limiter, the halving line search and the renormalisation of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-update.
6. After the loop, rebuild the active set and the gain at the final state, encode `diag`.

@fig-ch04-equilibrate-tp-convergence shows the two regimes on a single water reaction: from a ten-fold
supersaturation the residual falls quadratically once below one, and from a strong undersaturation with cloud present
the vapour grows geometrically until the last step is clipped and the cloud is exactly zero. The warm start keeps
`reaction_set` and `nactive` between calls so that the first pass of the next call tests the previously active
reactions first; the result does not depend on it (@sec-ch04-drivers).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-equilibrate-tp-convergence
#| fig-cap: "The fixed-temperature, fixed-pressure adjustment of one water reaction, from the numpy port of the kernel. (a) Condensation from a ten-fold supersaturation at 280 K and 1 bar: the residual per outer iteration (green circles, logarithmic) against the default tolerance (dotted vermillion). (b) Evaporation of a cloud at 300 K and 1 bar when the whole inventory fits in the vapour: vapour (blue circles) and cloud (dashed green triangles) mole fractions per iteration; the vapour grows by a factor near one plus the residual per pass, and the last step is clipped so that the cloud is exactly zero."
#| fig-alt: "Panel (a): the residual falls from about 2 to below 1e-11 over eight iterations, slowly over the first four and then very fast. Panel (b): the vapour fraction rises from 0.001 to 0.021 over about ten iterations while the cloud fraction falls from 0.02 to zero."
#| echo: false
from kintera_report.ch04.figures.fig_equilibrate_tp_convergence import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The cells are independent, so the driver runs the kernel per cell under a tensor iterator with a grain size of the
cell count over the thread count on CPU ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_dispatch.cpp call_equilibrate_tp_cpu >}}) and one
thread per cell on CUDA ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_dispatch.cu >}}, the subject of @sec-ch12). The kernel's
workspace is a per-cell arena (`pmalloc`) whose size is fixed by $N$ and $N_{\mathrm r}$ (`[C4]` of `drivers_check.py`).

: Code map of the fixed-temperature, fixed-pressure solver. {#tbl-ch04-equilibrate-tp-code}

Walk-through of `ThermoXImpl::forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::forward >}}):

1. No reactions: return an undefined tensor (the no-op).
2. Allocate `gain` $(\dots, N_{\mathrm r}^2)$ and, unless the caller passed one, `diag` $(\dots, 1)$; decide whether the
   saved active set can be reused (@sec-ch04-drivers), else reset it to the identity order with `nactive` $= 0$.
3. Build the tensor iterator over the cells with `gain`, `diag` and `xfrac` as outputs and $T$, $p$, `reaction_set`,
   `nactive` as inputs; build the curve kinds and parameters; dispatch to the device kernel with `ftol` and
   `max-iter`.
4. Return `gain` viewed as $(\dots, N_{\mathrm r}, N_{\mathrm r})$; `xfrac` was adjusted in place.

The kernel's own input checks print to standard output and return status 1: a non-positive $T$ or $p$, a negative
gas fraction, no gas at all; a negative condensate amount is set to zero with a warning. In Python:

```python
diag = torch.zeros(temp.shape + (1,), dtype=torch.float64)
gain = tx.forward(temp, pres, xfrac, False, diag)   # xfrac adjusted in place
failed = (diag[..., 0] < 0).sum()
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `max-iter` (default 10) is shared with the Newton loops of @sec-ch03; the tests that need it raise it to 15, 20 or
  50, and the deep-Jupiter card to 200. A cell that reaches the cap is returned partially adjusted and the kernel
  prints `did not converge` to standard output once per cell, which on CUDA is a device printf.
- The first phase from a strong undersaturation is slow (a factor $1 + |r|$ per pass on the vapour), so a card whose
  default `max-iter` is 10 can fail on evaporation from a very dry state; not measured on a realistic column.
- The solver is a local method: with several condensates competing for one vapour it converges to a point that
  satisfies the complementarity conditions, not necessarily the global minimum of the Gibbs energy; the in-tree
  note states the same caveat. Not measured.
- Input checks print and return status 1 instead of throwing; a host that ignores `diag` and standard output
  does not see them.
- The kernel's per-cell workspace is fixed by $N$ and $N_{\mathrm r}$; on CUDA a card with many condensables needs
  a smaller block (@sec-ch12, `test_cuda_workspace.py`).
:::
